properties.name: frontend.url
properties.description: Frontend application URL used for CORS allowed-origins and OAuth2 redirect configuration.

properties.name: backend.url
properties.description: Backend base URL used for generating self-referencing links and OAuth2 callback URLs.

properties.name: oauth.google.client-id
properties.description: Google OAuth2 client ID(s) from Google Cloud Console (APIs & Services, Credentials). Comma-separate several IDs (e.g. web, Android, iOS) to accept ID tokens issued to any of them.

properties.name: oauth.facebook.app-id
properties.description: Facebook OAuth2 app ID from Meta Developer Console.

properties.name: oauth.facebook.app-secret
properties.description: Facebook app secret, used to verify access tokens with /debug_token and to sign Graph API calls with appsecret_proof.

properties.name: oauth.github.client-id
properties.description: GitHub OAuth App client ID (GitHub, Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps).

properties.name: oauth.github.client-secret
properties.description: GitHub OAuth App client secret, used to exchange authorization codes and check access tokens.

properties.name: cloudinary.cloud-name
properties.description: Cloudinary account cloud name.

properties.name: cloudinary.api-key
properties.description: Cloudinary API key.

properties.name: cloudinary.api-secret
properties.description: Cloudinary API secret.

properties.name: jwt.secret
properties.description: Base64-encoded secret key used to sign and verify JWT tokens. Must match across all services.

properties.name: jwt.expiration
properties.description: JWT token expiration duration in milliseconds. Default is 30 days (2592000000).

properties.name: rate-limit.requests-per-minute
properties.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute per client before rate limiting kicks in.

properties.name: email.support
properties.description: Support email address used as the sender for outgoing application emails.

properties.name: profile-views.max-history-size
properties.description: Maximum number of profile view history entries to retain per user.

properties.name: app.api-key
properties.description: Shared secret API key required on the X-API-Key header to access protected public endpoints (e.g. /profile/public/directory). Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32. Set via the API_KEY environment variable in production — never commit the real value.

properties.name: app.security.initial-admin-emails
properties.description: Comma-separated emails provisioned as ADMIN at startup. A verified account is promoted; an address with no account gets an unverified admin account and an invitation email with a single-use link. Entries are trimmed, lower-cased, validated and de-duplicated. Removing an address never demotes an existing admin. (env INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS)

properties.name: app.security.auto-admin-emails
properties.description: Comma-separated emails that become ADMIN automatically once the account's email is verified (registration, sign-in, social login or account linking). (env AUTO_ADMIN_EMAILS)

properties.name: app.security.invitation-ttl-hours
properties.description: Hours an administrator invitation link stays valid. (env SECURITY_INVITATION_TTL_HOURS)

properties.name: app.security.login-email-notifications
properties.description: Send an email for sign-ins that need the owner's attention. (env SECURITY_LOGIN_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS)

properties.name: app.security.new-device-alerts
properties.description: Email the owner when an account signs in from a device not seen before. (env SECURITY_NEW_DEVICE_ALERTS)

properties.name: app.security.suspicious-login-alerts
properties.description: Email the owner when a sign-in scores above the risk alert threshold. Nothing is blocked automatically. (env SECURITY_SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_ALERTS)

properties.name: app.security.device-alert-cooldown-hours
properties.description: Hours before a recognised but untrusted device triggers another alert. 0 alerts on every sign-in. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_ALERT_COOLDOWN_HOURS)

properties.name: app.security.alert-first-device
properties.description: Also alert for the very first device of a brand new account. (env SECURITY_ALERT_FIRST_DEVICE)

properties.name: app.security.display-zone
properties.description: Time zone used to print times in security emails, for example UTC or Africa/Nairobi. (env SECURITY_DISPLAY_ZONE)

properties.name: app.security.security-page-path
properties.description: Path of the account security page on the frontend, linked from security emails. (env SECURITY_PAGE_PATH)

properties.name: app.security.device-trust-enabled
properties.description: Let users mark devices as trusted, which suppresses new-device alerts for them. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_TRUST_ENABLED)

properties.name: app.security.session-revocation-enabled
properties.description: Let users and administrators revoke sessions, which also invalidates their refresh tokens. (env SECURITY_SESSION_REVOCATION_ENABLED)

properties.name: app.security.device-cookie-name
properties.description: Name of the cookie that identifies a browser as a known device. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_COOKIE_NAME)

properties.name: app.security.device-cookie-secure
properties.description: Mark the device cookie Secure (https only). Set false only for plain-http local development. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_COOKIE_SECURE)

properties.name: app.security.device-cookie-same-site
properties.description: SameSite attribute of the device cookie: Lax, Strict or None. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_COOKIE_SAME_SITE)

properties.name: app.security.device-cookie-max-age-days
properties.description: Days the device cookie lives in the browser. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_DAYS)

properties.name: app.security.max-devices-per-user
properties.description: Most known devices kept per user. The least recently used are dropped beyond this. (env SECURITY_MAX_DEVICES_PER_USER)

properties.name: app.security.session-ttl-days
properties.description: Days a session and its refresh token live without being revoked. (env SECURITY_SESSION_TTL_DAYS)

properties.name: app.security.reauth-window-minutes
properties.description: Minutes after a social sign-in during which the session counts as freshly authenticated for sensitive actions. (env SECURITY_REAUTH_WINDOW_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.access-token-minutes
properties.description: Lifetime of access tokens in minutes. 0 keeps jwt.expiration (about 30 days) so current clients keep working. 15 to 60 is recommended once clients use the refresh token. (env SECURITY_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.hide-existing-accounts
properties.description: When true, POST /auth/signup answers the same for new and already-registered emails (202, no tokens) and tells the existing owner by email. When false the response says the email already exists. (env SECURITY_HIDE_EXISTING_ACCOUNTS)

properties.name: app.security.legacy-refresh-enabled
properties.description: Still accept an unexpired access token at POST /auth/refresh (older clients). Set false once clients use refresh tokens. (env SECURITY_LEGACY_REFRESH_ENABLED)

properties.name: app.security.trusted-proxies
properties.description: Comma-separated IPs or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For header is trusted. Empty trusts none, which is right when the service is reached directly. (env SECURITY_TRUSTED_PROXIES)

properties.name: app.security.ip-geolocation-enabled
properties.description: Look up an approximate location for sign-in IPs. Off by default because it sends visitor IP addresses to the provider in ip-geolocation-url. (env SECURITY_IP_GEOLOCATION_ENABLED)

properties.name: app.security.ip-geolocation-url
properties.description: URL template for the location lookup; {ip} is replaced by the address. (env SECURITY_IP_GEOLOCATION_URL)

properties.name: app.security.ip-geolocation-timeout-ms
properties.description: Milliseconds to wait for the location lookup before giving up. (env SECURITY_IP_GEOLOCATION_TIMEOUT_MS)

properties.name: app.security.audit-retention-days
properties.description: Days security audit events and sign-in records are kept before the daily clean-up removes them. (env SECURITY_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS)

properties.name: app.security.device-retention-days
properties.description: Days an unused known device is kept before the daily clean-up removes it. (env SECURITY_DEVICE_RETENTION_DAYS)

properties.name: app.security.login-max-failures
properties.description: Failed sign-ins for one account within the failure window before it is temporarily locked. (env SECURITY_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES)

properties.name: app.security.login-failure-window-minutes
properties.description: Minutes over which failed sign-ins for one account are counted. (env SECURITY_LOGIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.login-lockout-minutes
properties.description: Minutes of the first lock on an account. Repeated locks grow progressively up to the maximum. (env SECURITY_LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.login-max-lockout-minutes
properties.description: Longest lock on an account, in minutes. (env SECURITY_LOGIN_MAX_LOCKOUT_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.ip-max-failures
properties.description: Failed sign-ins from one IP address within the IP window before that address is throttled. (env SECURITY_IP_MAX_FAILURES)

properties.name: app.security.ip-max-distinct-accounts
properties.description: Different accounts one IP address may fail against within the IP window before it is throttled. (env SECURITY_IP_MAX_DISTINCT_ACCOUNTS)

properties.name: app.security.ip-window-minutes
properties.description: Minutes over which failures from one IP address are counted. (env SECURITY_IP_WINDOW_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.risk-alert-threshold
properties.description: Score out of 100 at which a sign-in is treated as suspicious and the owner is alerted. (env SECURITY_RISK_ALERT_THRESHOLD)

properties.name: app.security.location-change-window-hours
properties.description: Hours within which a change of country between sign-ins raises the risk score. (env SECURITY_LOCATION_CHANGE_WINDOW_HOURS)

properties.name: app.security.frequency-threshold
properties.description: Sign-ins within the frequency window that raise the risk score. (env SECURITY_FREQUENCY_THRESHOLD)

properties.name: app.security.frequency-window-minutes
properties.description: Minutes over which sign-in frequency is counted. (env SECURITY_FREQUENCY_WINDOW_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.distinct-ip-threshold
properties.description: Different IP addresses within the distinct-IP window that raise the risk score. (env SECURITY_DISTINCT_IP_THRESHOLD)

properties.name: app.security.distinct-ip-window-minutes
properties.description: Minutes over which different IP addresses are counted. (env SECURITY_DISTINCT_IP_WINDOW_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.action-token-ttl-minutes
properties.description: Minutes a "This wasn't me" link in a security email stays valid (default 24 hours). (env SECURITY_ACTION_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES)

properties.name: app.security.retention-cron
properties.description: Spring cron expression for the daily clean-up of old audit events, sign-in records and devices. (env SECURITY_RETENTION_CRON)

properties.name: app.admins.enabled
properties.description: Master switch for the administrators created at startup from ADMIN1_*, ADMIN2_* and ADMIN3_* (env ADMINS_ENABLED). When false no administrator is created from these settings.

properties.name: app.admins.strict
properties.description: When true, an invalid ADMINn slot stops the application from starting and nothing is created (env ADMINS_STRICT). When false the invalid slot is skipped and the reason is logged without any value.

properties.name: app.admins.promote-existing
properties.description: When true, an existing verified, active, non-administrator account with the same email as a slot is promoted to ADMIN; its password is never changed (env ADMINS_PROMOTE_EXISTING). When false it is left alone and a warning is logged, so configuration alone never raises an account's privileges.

properties.name: app.admins.min-password-length
properties.description: Minimum length of a configured administrator password (env ADMINS_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH). Values below 8 are raised to 8.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.email
properties.description: Sign-in email of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_EMAIL). Sign-in is by email, so a used slot needs it. Trimmed and lower-cased. Leave the whole slot empty to leave it unused.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.username
properties.description: Public handle of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_USERNAME). 3 to 30 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, lower-cased. Optional: when empty one is generated from the name. It is not used to sign in.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.first-name
properties.description: First name of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_FIRST_NAME). Required for a used slot.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.middle-name
properties.description: Middle name of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_MIDDLE_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.last-name
properties.description: Last name of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_LAST_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin1.password
properties.description: Password of administrator 1 (env ADMIN1_PASSWORD). SENSITIVE: supply it only through .env or the environment and never commit it. No default. At least 8 characters (at most 72 bytes), two of lower case, upper case, digits and symbols, not a well-known password and not containing the email or username. Stored only as a BCrypt hash, never logged, and ignored for an account that already exists. Change it after the first sign-in.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.email
properties.description: Sign-in email of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_EMAIL). Sign-in is by email, so a used slot needs it. Trimmed and lower-cased. Leave the whole slot empty to leave it unused.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.username
properties.description: Public handle of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_USERNAME). 3 to 30 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, lower-cased. Optional: when empty one is generated from the name. It is not used to sign in.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.first-name
properties.description: First name of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_FIRST_NAME). Required for a used slot.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.middle-name
properties.description: Middle name of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_MIDDLE_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.last-name
properties.description: Last name of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_LAST_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin2.password
properties.description: Password of administrator 2 (env ADMIN2_PASSWORD). SENSITIVE: supply it only through .env or the environment and never commit it. No default. At least 8 characters (at most 72 bytes), two of lower case, upper case, digits and symbols, not a well-known password and not containing the email or username. Stored only as a BCrypt hash, never logged, and ignored for an account that already exists. Change it after the first sign-in.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.email
properties.description: Sign-in email of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_EMAIL). Sign-in is by email, so a used slot needs it. Trimmed and lower-cased. Leave the whole slot empty to leave it unused.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.username
properties.description: Public handle of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_USERNAME). 3 to 30 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, lower-cased. Optional: when empty one is generated from the name. It is not used to sign in.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.first-name
properties.description: First name of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_FIRST_NAME). Required for a used slot.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.middle-name
properties.description: Middle name of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_MIDDLE_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.last-name
properties.description: Last name of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_LAST_NAME). Optional.

properties.name: app.admins.admin3.password
properties.description: Password of administrator 3 (env ADMIN3_PASSWORD). SENSITIVE: supply it only through .env or the environment and never commit it. No default. At least 8 characters (at most 72 bytes), two of lower case, upper case, digits and symbols, not a well-known password and not containing the email or username. Stored only as a BCrypt hash, never logged, and ignored for an account that already exists. Change it after the first sign-in.

properties.name: app.storage.type
properties.description: Where Home Owner application documents are stored (env STORAGE_TYPE): LOCAL is a directory on this server, NETWORK is a network share such as a Synology NAS that the operating system has mounted at app.storage.network.mount-path.

properties.name: app.storage.create-directories
properties.description: Create the storage directory when it does not exist (env STORAGE_CREATE_DIRECTORIES). Never applies to a network share that is not mounted.

properties.name: app.storage.fail-on-unavailable
properties.description: When true, an unusable storage location stops the application from starting (env STORAGE_FAIL_ON_UNAVAILABLE). When false it only logs a warning and document uploads answer 503 until the location works.

properties.name: app.storage.min-free-mb
properties.description: Uploads are refused while less than this many megabytes are free at the storage location (env STORAGE_MIN_FREE_MB). 0 turns the check off.

properties.name: app.storage.local.path
properties.description: Directory for LOCAL storage (env STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH). An absolute path, or one starting with ~/ for the home directory of the user running the service. Set it in .env for a specific folder; a blank value keeps the default.

properties.name: app.storage.network.protocol
properties.description: How the NAS share is mounted (env STORAGE_NETWORK_PROTOCOL): SMB (CIFS) or NFS. Used to recognise the right mount.

properties.name: app.storage.network.host
properties.description: IP address or host name of the NAS, for example a Synology on the LAN (env STORAGE_NETWORK_HOST). Used only to check that the right share is mounted; the application never connects to it and holds no NAS credentials. Empty checks just that something is mounted at the mount path.

properties.name: app.storage.network.share
properties.description: SMB: the share name. NFS: the exported path, for example /volume1/premisave (env STORAGE_NETWORK_SHARE). Used to check the mount.

properties.name: app.storage.network.mount-path
properties.description: Absolute path where the operating system mounted the share (env STORAGE_NETWORK_MOUNT_PATH). The NAS username and password belong to that mount (a root-only credentials file), not to this application.

properties.name: app.storage.network.directory
properties.description: Folder inside the mounted share that holds the documents (env STORAGE_NETWORK_DIRECTORY). A relative path without .. segments. Empty uses the root of the share.

properties.name: app.storage.network.require-mount
properties.description: Refuse to read or write unless the share is really mounted at the mount path (env STORAGE_NETWORK_REQUIRE_MOUNT). Keeps files from silently landing on the local disk when the NAS is unmounted. Turn off only for local development.

properties.name: spring.cloud.discovery.enabled
properties.description: Disables Spring Cloud service discovery (Eureka/Consul). Set to false when running without a service registry.

properties.name: home-owner-application.max-file-size-mb
properties.description: Largest accepted upload, in megabytes. Keep it below spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size.

properties.name: home-owner-application.max-documents
properties.description: Most files one application may hold.

properties.name: home-owner-application.review-sla-days
properties.description: Working days quoted to applicants as the usual review time.

properties.name: home-owner-application.max-reapplications
properties.description: How many times an applicant may reopen a rejected application to correct it and reapply (env HOME_OWNER_MAX_REAPPLICATIONS). 0 turns reapplying off. A reviewer can also close a single application for good when rejecting it.

properties.name: home-owner-application.frontend-path
properties.description: Frontend path the emails link to.

values.description: Suppresses hostname resolution warnings from Spring Cloud.
A network share (for example a Synology NAS) mounted by the operating system.
